{"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"A session can find out what designs exist nearby and be told which one to use, rather than inheriting one from where the shell happened to be","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Which design a session writes to must be a STATED CHOICE, and the information needed to make that choice must be available BEFORE anything is created. Two halves: (1) an agent must be able to discover what designs exist in and around a working tree and what each one holds — label, size, when it was minted — without opening a session against each; (2) a session must be able to be pointed at a chosen design explicitly.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-05, after the hxm_program field report: "can we just pass the location of the reflow2 graph via a prompt or skill; it can default to whichever folder path that the session is opened in, but maybe we could just say 'use reflow2 graph as /path/to/reflow2/graph/to/use/for/this/session'." And on the mechanism, once told a skill could not do it alone: "I like this approach of just pointing .mcp.json at the graph_id... an agent within a session can usually change files. can a reflow2 tool be to simply return all graph_ids to the agent and the agent then can choose whichever graph_id the user specifies to use for the project?"

WHY IT IS A REQUIREMENT AND NOT A CONVENIENCE. Today the answer is implicit: `.mcp.json` passes a RELATIVE `--graph-path`, so the design a session edits is decided by where the shell was opened, with no ancestor walk and no report of what else exists. Measured consequence, on Anthony's own repo the same day: a session at the root was told "this directory has no design yet" and minted a THIRD graph while two populated ones sat one and two directories down (`dec:no-design-here-never-looked`). An implicit answer to "which design am I editing" is not a smaller version of an explicit one — it is the mechanism by which a design gets created in the wrong place and nobody is told.

THE DIVISION OF LABOUR THIS INHERITS, and it shapes the answer rather than limiting it: reflow2 performs NO FILE IO (`dec:agent-navigates-content`), so WALKING THE TREE TO FIND `.reflow2` DIRECTORIES IS THE AGENT'S JOB — Anthony's own observation that "an agent within a session can usually change files" is the same point from the other side. What only reflow2 can answer is what a store at a given path actually HOLDS. So the requirement is met by a pair, not by one tool.

⚠️ MEASURED, AND IT CORRECTS THE OBVIOUS READING OF THE ASK: "return all graph_ids" would return ONE per store today. Storage keys are `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}` and `dynograph_storage::keys::graph_prefix` exists, so many graphs per store is supported by the FOUNDATION — but reflow2 opens one graph per store by convention (`DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID`, one `.reflow2` directory per project), and the three graphs in this field report are three separate STORES. Enumerating within a store is therefore true and not useful yet; describing a store found on disk is what the case actually needs.

NOT SETTLED HERE, deliberately: whether being "pointed at a design" means editing `.mcp.json` and reconnecting (cheap, works today, needs no release) or a graph reference carried per call (no reconnect, much larger). That is `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`.

Status `proposed`: captured in Anthony's words and awaiting his confirmation of the wording.","status":"proposed"}
